original_test_intent: Demonstrate each mapped DPU OOB port loses reachability when administratively/physically down, regains it when up and remains stable after five complete flap cycles.
original_method: Map DPU interface, physical port, peer and ping endpoints; retain independent management; preserve address/route/log baseline; operator performs an approved down/up action per port five times while automation timestamps link/carrier and ping results; confirm unchanged configuration and final recovery.
manual_activity: Operator controls the exact link fixture or approved DPU interface action for five cycles per port, observes physical state and restores management; agent only records bounded evidence.
required_inputs: Approved down/up mechanism and known ping endpoints
safety_requirements: Never flap the sole management path without alternate access
Do not alter addresses or routes
Preserve logs and full per-cycle evidence
Stop on unexpected reachability/configuration/recovery issue; no auto-retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate mapping, fixture and alternate access
Capture read-only baseline and synchronized per-cycle state/ping
Do not initiate an unapproved flap or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve ports, mechanism, endpoints and timing

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Read-only ip/route output is useful baseline evidence but cannot satisfy five down/up cycles; sshpass is rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Record target-bound `ip -d link`, address/route and bounded ping output before, during and after each operator-controlled flap.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Five cycles per port, up/down reachability behavior and 10-minute allocations are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a cycle-indexed state machine and synchronized interface/carrier/ping evidence while a human controls the disruptive action and alternate access.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact topology, timing oracle, alternate path, abort rules and final configuration diff.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A static route snapshot or LED note does not test flap recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Flapping OOB can sever the session or BMC path; peer/network behavior can confound ping.

project_override_considerations: Owner must specify administrative versus physical flap method, per-state dwell/ping timing, permitted packet loss and whether all OOB ports or one mapped port are required.
expected_evidence: Five indexed down/up link and ping results per port
Final unchanged configuration and restored BMC/OOB reachability

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master requires five disruptive down/up and ping cycles, while DeepSeek limits itself to a static read-only network snapshot and an unrelated LED observation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete; execution blocks without exact topology, safe flap mechanism, alternate access, operator and recovery oracle.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row391 Wistron-Networking-00380-V003: approve each DPU OOB interface/physical-port/peer/ping endpoint, administrative versus physical flap mechanism, five-cycle dwell/ping/loss oracle, alternate management path, operator control, abort/recovery and final configuration checks.

review_improvement: Converts a vague repeat instruction into five attributable, safely recoverable state transitions with per-cycle evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A ping result is meaningful only when tied to the exact interface, peer, route and carrier state. Because the interface under test may carry management itself, an independent access path and human-controlled abort are prerequisites; static enumeration cannot demonstrate recovery durability.
